raw_findings.fix: Note that only the two |t|>9 cells are established and the mirror's other diagonal is within noise; the orthogonality conclusion can rest on magnitude bounds (all <0.06 sd) alone.

raw_findings.line_hint: sec:staged, listed-after-round paragraph and financing-rows footnote
raw_findings.quote:
Among owners who did raise one, the same measure predicts
\emph{reaching} the public market: $+0.49$pp on a 3.49\% base, about 14\%
relative ($t = 3.8$).
raw_findings.issue: The listed-after-round result (t=3.8, n=38,886, on Form D data the paper itself calls provisional, after a construction choice — restricting to post-notice registrations — that halved the coefficient) is a marginal, heavily conditioned estimate presented as the payoff of the financing analysis; it belongs in the exploratory tier.
raw_findings.evidence: Three stacked fragilities are each stated separately (provisional raw extracts not in tree; survivor conditioning 'cannot separate... from selection on unobservables'; the 56% pre-round-listing exclusion halving the coefficient) but the headline sentence and the investor-screen interpretation carry none of them; jointly they make t=3.8 on one specification weak evidence.
raw_findings.fix: Label the row exploratory pending the Form D re-extract, and report the coefficient's sensitivity to the post-dating restriction (both halves) rather than only the restricted version.

raw_findings.quote: The pioneers are the ones with arrows in their backs. The saying is older than any dataset, and it has never been tested on the record where the claim could be read directly
raw_findings.issue: The opening priority claim ('never been tested') is contradicted by prior work in the paper's own bibliography: Semadeni & Anderson 2010 (AMJ 53(5):1175-1193) tested innovation vs imitation of new-offering language using US trademark/service-mark filings (top-50 consulting firms, 1989-1999), and Semadeni 2006 (SMJ 27:169-187) measured competitive positioning distance in service-mark language.
raw_findings.evidence: OpenAlex: the 2009 AMBPP version of Semadeni & Anderson states results 'derived from the U.S. Trademark database' on first-mover advantage and follower imitation; both papers are in bibliography.tex (keys Semadeni2006, SemadeniAnderson2010) yet the only cite keys used anywhere in v3 tex are Murdock2017, Barron2018, Graham2013, Seip2018, PatentsView.
raw_findings.fix: Qualify the priority claim to what is actually new (census scale, dated prosecution events, direction of vocabulary movement) and cite Semadeni 2006 / Semadeni & Anderson 2010 as the small-sample antecedent that did read positioning from the trademark record.

raw_findings.line_hint: whole file vs cite keys used
raw_findings.quote: \bibitem[Zhao et al.(2017)]{Zhao2017} ... Optimal distinctiveness: Broadening the interface between institutional theory and strategic management
raw_findings.issue: Every claimed disagreement in notes/claims_positioning.md exists only in the notes: none of the disagreement targets (Zhao 2017 optimal distinctiveness, Zuckerman 1999, Hsu 2006, Pontikes 2012, Mendonca 2004, Golder & Tellis 1993, Min et al. 2006) is cited anywhere in the v3 body, and Zuckerman, Hsu, Pontikes, Mendonca 2004, Golder & Tellis, and Min et al. are not even in bibliography.tex, so the paper's claimed contributions-by-disagreement are unverifiable from the draft itself.
raw_findings.evidence: grep of \cite commands across paper/v3/*.tex returns exactly five keys (Murdock2017 x2, Seip2018, PatentsView, Graham2013, Barron2018); Zhao2017 sits in the bibliography uncited; the intro (lines 33-44, 56-66, 88-96) asserts the examiner-vs-market inverse-U contrast and the pioneer-penalty positioning without naming any of the literatures they disagree with.
raw_findings.fix: Either engage the disagreement targets in the text with citations (registration inverse-U vs Zhao et al. 2017; spanning vs Zuckerman/Hsu/Pontikes; pioneer penalty vs Golder & Tellis 1993 and Min et al. 2006) or strike the positioning claims from notes so the contribution statement matches the draft.

raw_findings.quote: Category-spanning penalty (Zuckerman/Hsu/Pontikes [?]): theme importers survive better raw; penalty only net of atypicality. Spanning protects through the channel the literature says is costly.
raw_findings.issue: Listing Pontikes among the works disagreed with is not fairly stated: Pontikes 2012 (ASQ, 412 cites) herself shows ambiguous classification is MORE appealing to market-maker audiences (venture capitalists), so 'spanning protects for some audiences' is her finding, not her position being overturned; the theme-import protection result aligns with Pontikes rather than contradicting her.
raw_findings.evidence: OpenAlex abstract of doi:10.1177/0001839212446689: 'organizations that claim ambiguous labels are less appealing to consumers... but more appealing to venture capitalists, who are market-makers.' The gate (a market/commerce outcome) rewarding importers is a same-direction result for a non-consumer audience.
